name: _cast_Byte
description: Representative ATen schema (verbatim): aten::_cast_Byte(Tensor self, bool non_blocking=False) -> Tensor. This is the representative overload only and is NOT exclusive; the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must not be narrowed to this signature. All supplied registered schema strings (verbatim): aten::_cast_Byte(Tensor self, bool non_blocking=False) -> Tensor. Semantics: unary cast that converts an input tensor to torch.uint8; the only declared parameter is the non_blocking bool (default False), which does not change the computed values. Tests exercise integral (int8, uint8, int32, int64, bool), float (float16, bfloat16, float32, float64) and float8 (e4m3fn, e5m2) inputs, including offset, transposed and strided views (base[1:], base.t(), base[:, ::2], base[1:, ::3]), empty shapes, fractional, out-of-range and non-finite float values whose uint8 result is taken from the native result on the device (neither clamped nor widened), and special values. Because the operator declares no .out form and is unary, there is no broadcasting or out-variant coverage. Error behavior stays in pytest: a missing operand and a non-tensor input raise TypeError/RuntimeError, and a string, list or dict passed as non_blocking is rejected (None/0/1/1.5 are accepted natively). Alias/mutation is overload- and dtype-conditional and is therefore not modelled here: the selected schema declares no mutation and no argument aliases, while pytest additionally asserts that an already-uint8 input returns a same-device result sharing the input's data_ptr (identity/no-copy); this conditional effect is described only and not encoded in effects.
